summary: # 🚀 Geti™ v3.2.0 Geti 3.2 introduces many new classification models and various enhancements for dataset management and inference, as well as stability and performance improvements. To upgrade from an existing Geti™ 3.x deployment to 3.2, follow the [upgrade guide](https://github.com/open-edge-platform/geti/blob/0b8b22bbb8a7fc9f07eb8eaea7803f5259f5ea59/application/docs/upgrade.md). ## ✨ Highlights - **Pytorch Image Models (timm)** – 1600+ classification models from [_timm_](https://huggingface.co/timm) are now available in Geti™ and ready for fine-tuning, optimization and inference. - **Dataset views** – organize and filter your dataset flexibly by creating dataset views, custom subsets where you have full control over the assignment of dataset items. - **Configurable confidence threshold** – adjust the confidence threshold when requesting predictions in the annotator and when configuring a model in the inference pipeline. - **Quick ‘Annotation vs prediction’ comparison** – view the predictions generated by a trained model while remaining in the ‘Models’ page (‘Training datasets’ tab) and compare them with the respective annotations in one click. - **More reliable ‘Auto-segmentation’** – this annotation tool is now more stable and responsive thanks to several optimizations and fixes. ## 🗂️ Projects, datasets and annotation - **Dataset views** – the ‘Dataset’ page now offers the possibility to create and manage dataset views. Think of a view as a way to define a custom subset within your dataset, grouping media that have a specific property in common (e.g. photos taken at night). You can freely assign (and unassign) media to one or more dataset views, rename them, and of course filter the dataset by view. In a future version, Geti™ will also allow you to use dataset views as input for various workflows such as model fine-tuning and dataset export. - **Configurable confidence threshold (annotator)** – in the ‘Prediction’ tab you can now adjust the threshold value used to filter predictions based on their confidence score. Lowering the value allows you to see more predictions, while increasing it may help sometimes to filter out false positives. This option is available for all detection and segmentation models. - **Improved project list layout** – the ‘Project’ screen was optimized to display more projects in the available area. - **Inference settings icon** - in the ‘Prediction’ tab, all inference-related parameters have been grouped under a cogwheel icon. - **Bulk selection of media** - in the ‘Dataset’ page, use "CTRL + Left click" to add an item to the selection, and "Shift + Left click" to select a range of items. - **More annotator hotkeys** – Use “Left” and “Right” arrows to navigate between media while in the annotator, “Enter” to submit annotations and “Tab” to cycle through different shapes. ## 🧠 Models and training - **Pytorch Image Models (timm)** – the classification task now offers more than 1600 models thanks to the integration with [‘timm’](https://huggingface.co/timm), a large collection of SOTA models and weights across 80+ architecture families. You can find these models listed under the “Other models (timm)” card in the training dialog for single-label and multi-label classification, along with a special selector to choose the backbone and variant. All models can be fine-tuned, optimized, used for inference and exported. Note that Geti™ only exposes ‘timm’ models with a source code license that is compatible with Apache 2.0; at the same time, license of the respective pretrained weights is displayed in the UI so that you can pick a suitable model for your use case. - **Annotation vs prediction** – in the ‘Models’ page, when opening any image from the ‘Training datasets’ tab, you can now switch between the ‘Annotation’ and ‘Prediction’ view to quickly assess how the model performs on that media. Arrow buttons are also available to conveniently navigate through the other media in the subset. - **Training device column** – in the ‘Models’ page, all models now report the device (CPU / GPU model) that was used to train them. - **Updated Edgecrafter license** – for all ECDet (EdgeCrafter) models, the license changed from “Apache 2.0” to “[EdgeCrafter license](https://github.com/Intellindust-AI-Lab/EdgeCrafter/blob/main/LICENSE.md)” to reflect a recent change in the licensing of the original implementation. ## ⚙️️ REST API changes Always refer to the [API docs](https://docs.geti.intel.com/docs/rest-api/openapi-specification) to see the full specification. Differences from the previous release: - Introduced several new endpoints to manage dataset views, most of which under `../dataset/views`. Filtering by view is possible through `../dataset/media?dataset_view_id={view_id}`. - `POST ../media:predict` now accepts an optional request parameter `confidence_threshold` to specify a custom confidence threshold to filter output predictions. - Endpoints `GET ../models` and `GET ../models/{id}` now return an `optimal_confidence_threshold` field for each model variant. - Endpoints `GET ../models` and `GET ../models/{id}` now return a `device` field describing the device used during training. - Introduced a new endpoint `GET ../media/{id}/embeddings` to get the embeddings generated by the Segment Anything model on a given image. - Deprecated `GET ../media/media:predict` route in favor of the simpler `GET ../media:predict`. Both endpoints share the same parameters and behavior. ## 🐞 Bug fixes - The ‘Auto-segmentation’ annotation tool should no longer time out on loading or randomly crash, thanks to various optimizations and reworks. - Models no longer disappear after the training subprocess crashes abruptly. As a side effect, this issue also made it more difficult for users to access the logs. - Mitigated an issue with thumbnails loading very slowly while scrolling through large datasets. - Accuracy-aware quantization no longer fails on multilabel classification projects and with some YOLO segmentation models. - Resolved various inefficiencies in the memory usage of the training job, thus mitigating issues where training fails due to OOM on lower-end platforms or with memory-intensive configurations (e.g. large batch size, tiling enabled, ...). - The ‘Models’ screen no longer displays stale information for model revisions with deleted weights. - When a training job fails, the traceback is now available in the model logs and readable through the UI. - Importing a COCO dataset with bbox-like annotations as a new classification project now correctly results in a multilabel project instead of multiclass. - Import a COCO dataset with bbox-like annotations to a segmentation project no longer discards annotations. - In the annotator, segmentation labels no longer show in the wrong position for images with very high resolution. - The annotator now correctly jumps to the next media in the gallery after submitting an annotation, instead of the first one. - The dataset date filter doesn’t glitch anymore with invalid inputs. - The dataset export menu no longer shows warnings when not applicable. - In the exported demo packages, the label colors now consistently match the ones shown in the application (annotator and inference screens). - The desktop application is now more stable and should no longer crash with WebView-related errors. - All links can be now correctly opened from the desktop app. - The ‘run-image’ Just recipe no longer returns an error if the previous container hasn't fully stopped yet and the `—reload` option is provided. ## 📖 Documentation - Consolidated installation and upgrade guides to [install.md](https://github.com/open-edge-platform/geti/blob/develop/application/docs/install.md) and [upgrade.md](https://github.com/open-edge-platform/geti/blob/develop/application/docs/upgrade.md), respectively. - Documented a technical [path](https://github.com/open-edge-platform/geti/blob/develop/application/docs/install.md#i-have-an-old-nvidia-gpu-does-geti-support-it) to install Geti with support for old Nvidia GPUs. - Extended the [‘Troubleshooting’](https://github.com/open-edge-platform/geti/blob/develop/application/docs/install.md#troubleshooting) section in the installation guide to cover common error scenarios. - Updated [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/open-edge-platform/geti/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md) file for developers who want to contribute to Geti™. ## ⬇️ Download this release > [!WARNING] > The MSIX images are currently being published, the links below may not work yet. Please try again in a few hours, thanks for your patience. **Windows Installer** (run Geti as a native Windows application, with prebuilt images for Intel® XPU, NVIDIA® CUDA, and CPU-only environments): Download [CPU-only version installer](https://storage.geti.intel.com/geti/packages/3.2.0/geti-cpu-3.2.0.msix). Download [Intel® XPU version installer](https://storage.geti.intel.com/geti/packages/3.2.0/geti-xpu-3.2.0.msix). Download [Nvidia® CUDA version installer](https://storage.geti.intel.com/geti/packages/3.2.0/geti-cuda-3.2.0.msix) **Docker Images** ``` ghcr.io/open-edge-platform/geti-cpu:3.2.0 ghcr.io/open-edge-platform/geti-xpu:3.2.0 ghcr.io/open-edge-platform/geti-cuda:3.2.0 ``` Refer to the [installation](https://github.com/open-edge-platform/geti/blob/develop/application/docs/install.md) and [upgrade](https://github.com/open-edge-platform/geti/blob/develop/application/docs/upgrade.md) documentation for more details, including advanced deployment scenarios. --- # Geti Library (getitune) v0.3.0 _getitune_ is the library that powers Geti training, export, optimization, and inference. This release centers on the timm integration, a corrected export contract for NMS-based models, and better benchmarking observability. The new release is available as a Pypi package ([`getitune`](https://pypi.org/project/getitune/)) or it can be installed from source following the [documentation](https://docs.geti.intel.com/docs/user-guide/library/get-started/installation). ## Key new features and improvements - **Full PyTorch Image Models (timm) support** — enhanced the generic timm wrapper to support both multiclass and multilabel classification through generic recipes. Users can now train, test, and export any supported timm model for either classification task with minimal recipe changes. - **Explicit NMS export contract** — engine.export(...) now accepts an export_nms parameter. By default, NMS-based detection and instance-segmentation models export raw outputs, while ModelAPI applies NMS based on the exported metadata. This avoids hardware-specific graph compatibility issues. - **Memory profiling in benchmarks** — benchmark runs now sample and report peak GPU memory usage (CUDA/XPU) and peak host memory usage (RSS) as dedicated metrics. - **Ready-to-use helper scripts** — added entry points under scripts/ for benchmark dataset preparation, training, testing, model export, and prediction. - **Dependency upgrades** — upgraded OpenVINO™ ModelAPI to 0.4.7 and Datumaro to 1.13.11, improving model loading, inference adapters, and dataset format handling. ## Refactoring and bug fixes - Fixed accuracy-aware quantization for YOLO11/YOLO26 segmentation models and multilabel classification and corrected the quantization validation function. - Fixed OpenVINO tiling validation and updated the GPU augmentation pipeline to adapt the tiling batch size, reducing the risk of out-of-memory failures. - Fixed issues with memory pinning and workers auto-configuration, reducing the overall memory footprint of model evaluation. - Fixed issues identified while running the benchmark suite at scale. - Fixed model initialization logic to load pre-trained weights more safely. - Various cleanups and fixes across focal loss, the F-measure metric, tile merging, and data configuration.

summary:
## 🌟 Summary

**Ultralytics 8.4.153** delivers a critical SAM3 initialization fix, improves validation reliability, clarifies INT8 export behavior, and expands Ultralytics Platform documentation and annotation capabilities. 🚀

## 📊 Key Changes

- **🛠️ Fixed SAM3 `compile=False` handling — PR #26189 by @glenn-jocher**
  - Converts the predictor option correctly before passing it to the SAM3 builder:
    - `False` disables compilation.
    - `True` enables the default compilation mode.
    - Explicit compilation mode strings are preserved.
  - Prevents unintended `torch.compile` activation and the resulting PyTorch 2.14 Dynamo error during SAM3 initialization.
  - Validated across all six Platform SAM models for HTTP and WebSocket inference.
  - Package version bumped to **8.4.153**.

- **✅ Improved standalone semantic segmentation validation**
  - Polygon-based semantic datasets now receive their background class metadata during dataset construction.
  - Prevents background pixels from being incorrectly assigned to the final real class.
  - Makes standalone validation metrics such as mIoU and pixel accuracy meaningful again.

- **🖼️ Fixed standalone classification validation with extra classes**
  - Validation now filters samples whose class IDs are outside the model’s class range, matching existing training behavior.
  - Prevents `IndexError` crashes when the validation dataset contains more classes than the checkpoint supports.
  - Clear warnings identify skipped samples and mismatched classes.

- **🔄 Preserved explicit datasets when resuming training**
  - `train(resume=True, data="...")` now correctly honors the user-provided dataset instead of silently using the checkpoint’s original dataset.
  - Path-based resumes also avoid injecting an unintended task-default dataset.

- **⚙️ Improved INT8 export behavior and documentation**
  - Quantization-aware training checkpoints can export their stored INT8 ranges without calibration data for ONNX and TensorRT.
  - RKNN INT8 validation now correctly applies to detection models only, including INT8-only Rockchip targets.
  - RKNN examples now use a compatible detection model and dataset.
  - TensorRT documentation no longer claims that `dynamic` is automatically enabled for INT8 exports.

- **🎯 Preserved `conf=0.0` during IMX export**
  - An explicit zero confidence threshold is no longer replaced with `0.001`.
  - Added coverage for both `conf=0.0` and the default `conf=0.25` behavior.

- **🧩 Expanded Platform annotation and billing documentation**
  - Added documentation for dataset-wide batch annotation, class mapping, progress tracking, stopping runs, version snapshots, and billing.
  - YOLO smart annotation now includes pose datasets, while SAM remains available for detection, segmentation, semantic, and OBB tasks.
  - Documented the Platform referrals tab, endpoint uptime charges, batch annotation pricing, supported dataset licenses, and Python 3.11 requirement.
  - Agents documentation now reflects that the feature no longer requires Early Access.

- **📚 Documentation and links updated**
  - Repository banners now link to the [YOLO27 preview and waitlist](https://www.ultralytics.com/yolo/yolo27).
  - Added Huawei Ascend and Google Coral Edge TPU to the Hailo hardware comparison.
  - Removed the unreachable retired Neptune integration page.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact

- **More reliable SAM3 deployments:** Users on newer PyTorch versions can initialize and run SAM3 without unexpected compilation or Dynamo failures. 🧠
- **More trustworthy validation results:** Semantic and classification validation now better reflect the actual model and dataset configuration.
- **Safer resume workflows:** Explicit dataset overrides are respected, reducing the risk of accidentally continuing training on the wrong data.
- **Simpler edge deployment:** INT8 export rules are clearer and better aligned with actual ONNX, TensorRT, and RKNN behavior.
- **More predictable export thresholds:** IMX users can intentionally disable filtering with `conf=0.0`.
- **Broader Platform workflows:** Pose smart annotation and batch annotation make dataset preparation faster, while updated billing and integration documentation makes Platform usage easier to understand.
- **Upgrade recommendation:** Users relying on SAM3, standalone validation, training resume, IMX export, or RKNN INT8 export should upgrade to **8.4.153**. 🔄

## What's Changed
* Update banner destination links to YOLO27 by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26177
* Align INT8 export, Platform Python floor and Hailo comparison docs with merged behavior by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26174
* Remove the unreachable Neptune integration page by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26170
* Fix standalone semantic val mislabeling background pixels as the last class by @cainiao33 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26176
* Preserve an explicit data= override when resuming training by @cainiao33 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26175
* Link the YOLO27 waitlist from the coming-soon notice by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26188
* Align Platform docs with dataset licenses, the referrals tab and pose smart annotation by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26185
* Document Platform batch annotation and its billing by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26186
* Fix the RKNN INT8 detect-only gate for INT8-only targets and its docs example by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26184
* Preserve conf=0.0 in IMX export score_threshold by @cainiao33 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26183
* Fix standalone classify val crash on datasets with extra classes by @cainiao33 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26182
* Fix SAM3 compile=False handling and release 8.4.153 by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26189


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.152...v8.4.153
